# A Shiny Color Survey

## Setting Up and a basic Overview

For this lab, we'll use the XKCD Color survey data.
The TidyTuesday documentation is available [here](https://github.com/rfordatascience/tidytuesday/blob/main/data/2025/2025-07-08/readme.md).




1. The responses to the color survey are the basis for the 2010 xkcd blog entry [Color Survey Results](https://blog.xkcd.com/2010/05/03/color-survey-results/). Read the blog entry, pick two of the described findings and (try to) reproduce them. Show your code. In case you fail to reproduce the described findings describe the obstacle(s) you ran into.


2. Colors are often reported in form of hexcodes. Hexcodes are a representation of the RGB (red green blue) color model and follow the format `#RRGGBB`, where `RR` stands for the amount of red in the color, coded as a hexadecimal number between 0 (= #00) and 255 (= #FF). Similarly, `GG` and `BB` encode the amount of green and blue in the color.

The RGB model allows to encode a total of $16^2 \times 16^2 \times 16^2 = 2^{24} = 16,777,216$ 'different' colors. 

Create a data frame `rgb_df` with variables `r`, `g`, and `b` on a regular grid (i.e. every 10th or every 16th value between 0 and 255). Use the function `rgb` to create a variable `hex` of hexcodes created from the `r`, `g`, and `b` values. Describe the resulting chart and remember to fill in the alt-text.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
# Your code goes here

rgb_df |> ggplot(aes(x = r, y = g)) + geom_point(aes(colour = hex)) + scale_colour_identity() + facet_wrap(~b)
```

3. An alternative to the RGB color model is the HCL model. It specifies the dimensions hue, chroma, and luminance. Use the function `decode_colour` from the `farver` package to create coordinates `h`, `c`, `l`. Include those coordinates in the data frame `rgb_df` and explore the HCL space visually, similarly to the previous question. Summarise your findings and write an appropriate figure caption and alt text for @fig-hcl.


::: {.cell}

## Now make it shiny

Create a `shiny` app in R centered around the xkcd survey. You can pick any aspect you want, but the resulting shiny app should be based on actual data, have at least one chart, and at least two user input widgets that allow the user to interact with the results shown in the chart.

Include the code for the app in the file `app.R`.
